answer: A memory-commitment protocol resists Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock dedicated VRAM partitions verified via latency-sensitive challenges. An attacker creating fake personas incurs the verifiable cost of holding physical memory offline per identity, halting an ocean of clones. Unregistered nodes remain restricted to an operational tundra. A key limitation is that an unexpected plume of verification traffic can saturate bus bandwidth and throttle honest nodes.
